course_title: Online Portfolio Building: Show Your Best Work and Win Clients

say: What to show in your portfolio, and why.
This is the video for module one of Online Portfolio Building.

say: Think of the busy person opening your link. She quietly asks four questions.
First, can she do what I need? She looks for work similar to her own job.

panel.heading: Four questions every viewer asks
items: Can she do what I need?
Is the quality good enough?
Can I trust her?
How do I reach her, and what will it cost?

say: Second, is the quality good enough? She looks closely at photos, finishing and detail.

panel.heading: Four questions every viewer asks
items: Can she do what I need?
Is the quality good enough?
Can I trust her?
How do I reach her, and what will it cost?

say: Third, can I trust her? She looks for real customers, results, testimonials, and a real name and face.

panel.heading: Four questions every viewer asks
items: Can she do what I need?
Is the quality good enough?
Can I trust her?
How do I reach her, and what will it cost?

say: Fourth, how do I reach her, and what will it cost? She looks for a clear contact button and a guide to your prices.
Your portfolio should answer all four without her needing to ask you.

say: For example, Ngozi is a tailor in Enugu. A new customer wants to see her work before ordering an aso ebi outfit.
First, Ngozi forwards 37 photos in one message. Some are blurry, some are not hers, and none say what the customer asked for.

panel.heading: Ngozi the tailor, two ways
left: Some blurry, some not her work

say: Then Ngozi sends one link to a simple free website with six pieces. Each has three clear photos, front, back and the beading detail, and four short lines about the job.
The customer messages her with the exact style she likes. The portfolio did the selling.

panel.heading: Ngozi the tailor, two ways
left: Some blurry, some not her work

say: Before you choose anything, write one sentence. Who is your portfolio for, and what should they do? For example, mothers planning children's parties who should message me to order a cake.

panel.heading: From many photos to a strong few
items: Write one sentence: who it is for, what they should do
Remove anything that is not your own work
Test each piece: is it good, and is it relevant?
Show range, not the same item six times
Put your strongest, most relevant piece first

say: Next, remove anything that is not your own work. Never use photos from Pinterest or a supplier's catalogue. Customers find out, and one copy can destroy all your trust.

panel.heading: From many photos to a strong few
items: Write one sentence: who it is for, what they should do
Remove anything that is not your own work
Test each piece: is it good, and is it relevant?
Show range, not the same item six times
Put your strongest, most relevant piece first

say: Then test each piece twice. Quality: is this among my best? Relevance: does it match the work I want more of?

panel.heading: From many photos to a strong few
items: Write one sentence: who it is for, what they should do
Remove anything that is not your own work
Test each piece: is it good, and is it relevant?

Put your strongest, most relevant piece first

say: Show range within your focus. Different occasions, sizes, budgets or colours tell the viewer you can handle her job.

panel.heading: From many photos to a strong few
items: Write one sentence: who it is for, what they should do

say: Put your strongest, most relevant piece first, and your second strongest last, because people remember endings.

say: The most common mistake is showing too much. A viewer remembers your weakest three pieces, so keep five to eight strong ones.

panel.rule: 5 to 8 strong pieces beat 30 mixed ones.

say: A portfolio is public, so protect your customers and yourself. Ask permission before you show a customer's face, name, home or event. A WhatsApp message is enough. Save the reply in a Permissions folder.

panel.heading: Privacy check for every image
items: Written permission saved
No phone numbers or receipts
No children's faces without consent
No bank, BVN or ID details
Your area only, not your home address
Team and practice work labelled honestly

say: Check every photo for phone numbers, addresses and receipts. Never show a child's face without the parent's clear permission. Never post your BVN, NIN, bank login or ID card.

panel.heading: Privacy check for every image
items: Written permission saved
No phone numbers or receipts
No children's faces without consent
No bank, BVN or ID details
Your area only, not your home address
Team and practice work labelled honestly

say: Show your area, like Surulere, Lagos, not your full address. And label honestly. If you worked in a team, name your part. If it was practice, say practice project.

say: To remember. A portfolio shows proof, not claims. Answer the four questions every viewer asks.
Choose five to eight strong, relevant pieces, best first. Show only your own work, labelled honestly. And protect privacy before you publish.

panel.heading: Remember
items: A portfolio shows proof; a CV only makes claims
